parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a two-stage Ligra then Ligra+ evolution in one /workspace tree, including framework primitives, applications, compression support, encoder/decoder, Makefile updates, run.sh, results.json, and required git commits.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although launched in parallel mode with swarm enabled, the run used a single main-agent work path. The evidence shows no delegation, no subagents, and no parallel uptake, so ownership remained local to the main trajectory.
parallel.implementation: Committed a Ligra baseline adding application sources and updating ligra/ligra.h, then committed Ligra+ additions including byte/byteRLE/nibble headers, compressedVertex updates, encoder/decoder, compressed graph data, run.sh, and results.json.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all changes directly in the existing workspace layout, kept the requirement-patches commits for ligra and ligra_plus, and delivered /workspace/results.json through run.sh output.
parallel.verification: The post-test run wrote bfs_level_count 6, triangle_count 107, compressed BFS 125, and PageRank sum 0.980078, and all Ligra and Ligra+ pytest cases passed in the current official evaluation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible unfinished requirement remained at closure. The only process caveat is that the nominal parallel run did not execute any child-agent mechanism, so it supplies no parallel coordination episode to classify.

serial.requirements: Received the same task prompt and requirement order: implement Ligra baseline first, extend the same workspace with Ligra+, update run.sh, write four numeric result values, and commit each requirement patch.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Ran as the serial control with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled, no delegation, no subagents, and all implementation owned by the main trajectory.
serial.implementation: Committed a Ligra baseline with framework/application changes and compiled app binaries, then committed Ligra+ compression files, encoder/decoder, compressed input, run.sh, results.json, and updated binaries.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated changes directly in the single workspace and delivered the required results.json and requirement patch commits for the two requirement slugs.
serial.verification: The post-test run wrote bfs_level_count 6, triangle_count 107, compressed BFS 125, and PageRank sum 0.9800781250, and all Ligra and Ligra+ pytest cases passed in the current official evaluation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible unfinished requirement remained at closure; the serial run is a valid non-delegating control and also passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed status evaluation is not discordant: both the nominal parallel run and the serial control pass. Both independently implemented the staged Ligra then Ligra+ work, committed the two required requirement slugs, generated the required four numeric experiment results, and passed the same official test set. The important annotation difference is that the parallel-mode run never executed a child-agent or multi-agent mechanism, so concurrency-error taxonomy retention is blocked by the first retention-gate condition rather than by a weaker label-specific near miss.

ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial git log includes compiled application binaries in commits while the parallel log emphasizes source/header changes; this did not affect the official outcome.
The two runs print PageRank sums with different precision, 0.980078 versus 0.9800781250, but both satisfy the evaluator.
